title: Navigation, toasts, modals, quick actions, and Flow integration
objectives: Choose lightning/navigation versus a toast, LightningModal, a screen or headless quick action, or a Flow screen component.
State the documented containers where lightning/navigation is not supported.
Prefer lightning/toast over platformShowToastEvent where the Guide says so, and explain LWR-site limits.
Capture recordId on an LWC screen quick action with an @api setter, not connectedCallback.
diagnostic_question: A stakeholder wants a button that confirms a Case close, tells the user it worked, then opens the Account. Which of navigation, toast, modal, quick action, or Flow do you pick for each step, and what would you not use in Lightning Out?
definition: Navigation, toasts, modals, quick actions, and Flow integration are the Lightning Web Components ways to move the user, announce an outcome, collect a blocking decision, host a record-page action, or embed admin-owned automation in a screen. The LWC Developer Guide's navigation service is lightning/navigation in Lightning Experience, Experience Builder sites, and the Salesforce mobile app—not Lightning Components for Visualforce or Lightning Out. Toasts prefer lightning/toast.show(); modals extend LightningModal; screen quick actions open a modal and close with CloseActionScreenEvent; Flow uses LWC as screen components or local actions. ([Navigate to Pages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-navigate.html); [Toast Notifications](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-toast.html); [Modal Windows](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-dialog-modal.html); [Screen Quick Actions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-quick-actions-screen.html); [Flows](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-flow.html))
why_it_matters: Wrong channel is a common interview fail: a toast for a destructive confirm, NavigationMixin on LightningModal, or reading recordId in connectedCallback on a quick action. Lightning Out and LWR sites silently lack some modules. Mixing Flow and LWC without a target configuration also ships a component admins cannot drop on a screen.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel concierge desk. Navigation is walking the guest to a room. A toast is a sticky note on the counter. A modal is a private conversation booth that blocks the lobby until they answer. A quick action is the front-desk bell that opens a standard request window. Flow is handing the guest to a specialist who already owns the checklist. You do not shout a sticky note when you need a signature, and you do not walk guests through a door that does not exist in that building (Lightning Out).
deeper_explanation: Use lightning/navigation with a PageReference to open records, lists, named pages, or URL-addressable LWCs. The service is not supported in Lightning Components for Visualforce or Lightning Out 2.0 / Lightning Out (beta), even if those containers sit inside Lightning Experience. LWR apps use lwr/navigation instead. lightning__UrlAddressable is not supported in Experience Builder sites. ([Navigate to Pages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-navigate.html))

lightning/toast with LightningToast.show() is the preferred toast API and supports inline links in title and message. lightning/platformShowToastEvent is event-based, lacks title links, and is not supported on Aura-site login pages, LWR Experience Cloud sites, or standalone apps. lightning/toastContainer can cap how many toasts appear. ([Toast Notifications](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-toast.html))

A modal extends LightningModal from lightning/modal—not LightningElement—and uses lightning-modal-header/body/footer. Open it with MyModal.open() from a parent. You cannot use NavigationMixin directly on the LightningModal class; navigate from a LightningElement parent (or a child that extends LightningElement) after the modal dispatches a PageReference. ([Modal Windows](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-dialog-modal.html); [Navigate From a Modal](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-navigate-modal.html))

Screen quick actions appear in a modal. Unlike other record-page LWCs, recordId is not ready in connectedCallback(); declare an @api setter that stores this._recordId. Close with CloseActionScreenEvent from lightning/actions. lightning-quick-action-panel supplies SLDS header/body/footer. Custom footer plus the X control skips Cancel logic. Headless quick actions run without a UI. ([Screen Quick Actions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-quick-actions-screen.html))

Flow integration means building LWC as flow screen components or flow local actions, with the matching targets and property editors. Do not reinvent an entire wizard in LWC when a Screen Flow already owns the business steps; do not drop a Flow inside LWC when you only needed a toast.

mental_model.analogy: A hotel concierge desk: escort to a room, sticky note, private booth, front-desk bell, specialist with a checklist.
useful_mapping: escort to a room → lightning/navigation PageReference
sticky note on the counter → toast (lightning/toast preferred)
private booth that blocks the lobby → LightningModal
front-desk bell → screen or headless quick action
specialist checklist → Flow screen component or local action
building with no concierge corridor → Lightning Out / Visualforce: no lightning/navigation
where_it_breaks: A hotel booth can still walk you to a room; LightningModal cannot call NavigationMixin itself.
A sticky note is not a confirm-delete; that needs a modal or Flow.
The bell on a record page delivers recordId later than connectedCallback.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I pick a channel: navigation to move, toast to announce, LightningModal to block, quick action for record chrome, Flow when admins own the steps. I never assume lightning/navigation works in Lightning Out.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the user moment. Confirm-delete is a modal or Flow, not a toast. After success I prefer lightning/toast, especially on LWR sites where platformShowToastEvent is unsupported. If I must navigate from a modal, the parent LightningElement calls NavigationMixin. On a screen quick action I capture recordId with a setter and close with CloseActionScreenEvent.

terminology.plain: The LWC service that opens another page, record, or list using a PageReference.
terminology.precise: Supported in Lightning Experience, Experience Builder sites, and the Salesforce mobile app. Not supported in Lightning Components for Visualforce or Lightning Out. LWR apps use lwr/navigation.
terminology.example: NavigationMixin.Navigate to a LAB_ Account record page after save.
terminology.non_example: window.location.assign to a Salesforce URL inside Lightning Out hoping it is the navigation service.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: lwr/navigation for Lightning Web Runtime apps.
terminology.boundary: PageReference type catalog is neighboring reference material.

terminology.plain: A temporary popup that announces success, error, warning, or info.
terminology.precise: Prefer LightningToast.show() from lightning/toast. platformShowToastEvent is not supported on LWR Experience sites, Aura login pages, or standalone apps.
terminology.example: After createRecord, a success toast with a link to the new LAB_ Account.
terminology.boundary: Inline error regions from LWC-007 still belong on the card.

terminology.plain: A custom overlay you open in code that blocks the rest of the page.
terminology.precise: Extend LightningModal from lightning/modal. There is no lightning-modal tag. Parent calls MyModal.open(). NavigationMixin is not used on the modal class itself.
terminology.non_example: A screen quick action you configured in Setup without extending LightningModal.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Screen quick action modal chrome via lightning-quick-action-panel.
terminology.boundary: Notification alert/confirm/prompt are sibling dialog helpers.

terminology.plain: An LWC that opens in a modal from a record or global action.
terminology.precise: Requires a quick-action target. recordId arrives via an @api setter, not connectedCallback. Close with CloseActionScreenEvent. Optional lightning-quick-action-panel for SLDS structure.
terminology.example: Update Phone action on LAB_ Contact using lightning-record-edit-form inside the panel.
terminology.non_example: Headless quick action with no UI.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: LightningModal.open from a button that is not an action.
terminology.boundary: Headless invoke details are the sibling headless page.

terminology.plain: An LWC an admin places on a Flow screen.
terminology.precise: Configured with Flow targets so Flow Builder can drop it on a screen or use it as a local action. Properties must match supported Flow data types.
terminology.example: A map picker LWC on a Screen Flow that updates a LAB_ Address.
terminology.non_example: Calling Apex from LWC and calling it 'Flow integration.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: lightning-flow host component—Needs verification of current embed APIs.
terminology.boundary: Whether the process should be Flow at all is AUTO-001.

terminology.plain: The event that closes an LWC screen quick action modal.
terminology.precise: Imported from lightning/actions. Use it for Cancel or after a successful save. The X control does not run your Cancel handler if you built a custom footer.
terminology.non_example: LightningModal.close() on a non-quick-action modal—that is this.close() on LightningModal.
terminology.boundary: Only for the quick-action screen target.

when_to_use: When you must move the user with lightning/navigation in Lightning Experience, an Experience Builder site, or the Salesforce mobile app.
When a short success or error announcement is enough: prefer a toast via lightning/toast, not a blocking modal.
When the user must confirm or complete a form in a blocking overlay: LightningModal or a screen quick action.
When admins own a multi-step process: Flow integration with an LWC screen component or local action rather than a hard-coded wizard.
when_not_to_use: Do not use lightning/navigation in Lightning Out, Lightning Components for Visualforce, or as a substitute for lwr/navigation in an LWR app.
Do not use platformShowToastEvent as your only toast on an LWR Experience Cloud site or standalone app.
Do not put NavigationMixin on a LightningModal class, or read recordId only in connectedCallback on a screen quick action.
Do not rebuild an entire Flow in LWC toasts and modals when a Screen Flow already fits, and do not skip LWC-007 inline error states by toasting every empty list.

Setup: object Quick Action pointing at the LWC, or Flow Builder screen.
Parent JS: MyModal.open() then Navigate from the callback.

decision_table.signal: User must confirm a destructive or irreversible Case close.
decision_table.choose: LightningModal or a screen quick action form, optionally a Screen Flow.
decision_table.not: A success toast that performs the close with no confirm.
decision_table.why: Toasts announce; they do not collect a blocking decision.

decision_table.signal: Save succeeded and the user should stay on the page.
decision_table.choose: lightning/toast show() with a short success message.
decision_table.not: platformShowToastEvent as the only option on an LWR Experience site.
decision_table.why: The Guide prefers lightning/toast and documents platformShowToastEvent gaps.

decision_table.signal: After the overlay, open the parent Account record in Lightning Experience.
decision_table.choose: NavigationMixin on a LightningElement parent (or the page component), not on LightningModal.
decision_table.not: Apply NavigationMixin directly to the LightningModal class.
decision_table.why: Navigate From a Modal requires a LightningElement to call the mixin.

decision_table.signal: The same form must appear from the record action bar.
decision_table.choose: Screen quick action with recordId setter and CloseActionScreenEvent.
decision_table.not: Rely on connectedCallback for recordId like a normal record-page LWC.
decision_table.why: The Screen Quick Actions topic documents that timing difference.

decision_table.signal: Admins must change steps without a code deploy.
decision_table.choose: Flow integration: LWC as a screen component or local action.
decision_table.not: Hard-code the wizard as nested LightningModal calls.
decision_table.why: The Flows topic exists so LWC participates in Flow Builder, not replaces every Flow.

interview_questions.question: How do you choose among navigation, toast, modal, quick action, and Flow in LWC?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Navigate to move, toast to announce, modal or screen action to block, Flow when admins own the steps. Check the container before using lightning/navigation.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I start from the user moment, not the API I like. Destructive confirm is never a toast. Record-page chrome often wants a screen quick action with a recordId setter. After success I toast, then navigate from a LightningElement if needed. If the wizard must change without deploys, I expose LWC to Flow instead of nesting modals.
interview_questions.example: Close LAB_ Case: screen action form, lightning/toast, then optional Navigate to Account from a parent.
weak_answer_warnings: One API for every UX problem

interview_questions.question: Where does lightning/navigation not work?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Lightning Components for Visualforce and Lightning Out, even if those containers are inside Lightning Experience. LWR apps need lwr/navigation.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I recite the support matrix from the Navigate topic. I do not promise deep-link LWC navigation in Lightning Out. For Experience Builder I also remember lightning__UrlAddressable is unsupported. Interviewers listen for that container humility.
interview_questions.example: A Visualforce page hosting Lightning Out cannot call NavigationMixin to a record page.

Custom URL component versus Experience site

interview_questions.question: Your modal must navigate to a record. How do you structure the components?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The modal extends LightningModal and fires an event with a PageReference. The parent extends NavigationMixin(LightningElement) and calls Navigate.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not put NavigationMixin on the modal class. The Navigate From a Modal topic is explicit. The child inside the modal may dispatch the PageReference; the parent that called MyModal.open handles onnavigate. That is the interview diagram.

Child versus modal dispatching the event

What page type do you use?

interview_questions.question: A screen quick action's form is empty. recordId looks undefined. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Whether you read recordId in connectedCallback. Use an @api setter into a private field and read that later.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Unlike other record-page LWCs, quick actions assign recordId after connectedCallback. I implement set recordId and get recordId, store _recordId, and wire or query from the setter. I also confirm the target is lightning__RecordAction / screen, not a normal page component dropped on the layout.
interview_questions.example: labEditPhone setter logs the Id after the first connectedCallback log shows undefined.
follow_ups: How do you close after save?
weak_answer_warnings: Blaming FLS before checking setter timing

interview_questions.question: Toasts work in the org app but not on an LWR site. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: platformShowToastEvent is not supported on LWR Experience Cloud sites. Switch to lightning/toast.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I ask which module they imported. If it is ShowToastEvent, that matches the documented gap. I migrate to LightningToast.show with the component as the second argument. I still keep inline errors on the form from LWC-007; a missing toast is not the only channel.
interview_questions.example: Experience Cloud LWR intake form: ShowToastEvent silent; lightning/toast visible.
weak_answer_warnings: Blaming CSP first without checking the toast module

interview_questions.question: Users click X on your quick action and unsaved work vanishes without your Cancel warning. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: With a custom footer, X only closes the modal. Cancel logic does not run. The Guide calls this out.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I either use lightning-quick-action-panel patterns that match platform Cancel, warn in UX copy, or avoid putting unique logic only on Cancel. I do not promise a beforeunload hook that the X control will honor. Interviewers like that you read the limitation instead of calling it a platform bug.
interview_questions.example: Custom Save/Cancel footer; X discards the LAB_ Phone edit silently.
tradeoffs: Custom footer styling versus platform close behavior
Warn on every field change versus accept the gap
weak_answer_warnings: Filing a Salesforce bug as the first answer

interview_questions.question: When is Flow the better host than a stack of LWC modals?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When admins must change steps, branching, or data writes without a JS deploy, and LWC only supplies a custom widget on a screen.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep AUTO-001 in mind: Flow owns the process. LWC supplies UI the base Flow screen cannot. I add the Flow screen target and supported property types. I do not hide a five-step intake behind nested LightningModal.open calls that only developers can change.
interview_questions.example: Address-picker LWC on a Screen Flow that creates a LAB_ Service Appointment.
follow_ups: What is a Flow local action?
How do you validate a custom screen component?
weak_answer_warnings: LWC for every wizard by default

interview_questions.question: Teach these five channels with a hotel-desk analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Escort is navigation, sticky note is toast, booth is modal, bell is quick action, specialist is Flow. The booth cannot walk you to the room—LightningModal cannot host NavigationMixin.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map each channel, then the breaks: Lightning Out has no corridor; LWR uses a different escort service; the bell delivers the room number after you already stepped into connectedCallback. That last point is the quick-action recordId trap.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard the Close Case path with four boxes and one 'not in Out' sticker.
